title: Add anomaly-anchored log summaries and operator dashboard
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds an operator-facing dashboard and anomaly-anchored log summarization pipeline to accelerate incident triage. Introduces a signal-to-noise scoring metric used to prioritize alerts and suppress noisy baselines. Rollout is staged behind a feature flag with canary -> 50% -> global expansion.
description: Context and motivation: On several recent incidents we observed long investigation times because traces with anomalous token-cost/latency patterns lacked compact contextual log snippets that were easy to scan. This PR introduces an "anomaly-anchor" concept: when the anomaly detector flags a spike, we capture a narrow time window around the anomalous invocation, synthesize a concise log summary (TL;DR), and surface it in a new operator dashboard alongside a prioritized incident queue. Goals: 1) reduce mean time to triage by surfacing concise context, 2) prioritize alerts by a signal-to-noise ratio so SREs focus on genuine regressions, 3) provide per-tenant baseline drift visualization to speed root cause identification.
changes_summary: This is a cross-cutting change touching the telemetry ingestion pipeline, runtime sidecar, and the Console dashboards. High-level list of changes: 1) telemetry/processor/anomaly_anchor.go: new service that listens for anomaly events, materializes a 30s window of logs/traces, runs a summarizer (n-gram + keyword extraction + concise template), and emits summary records. 2) runtime/sidecar/log_tldr.go: lightweight summarizer used at edge for low-batch scenarios to reduce downstream storage costs. 3) telemetry/catalog/metrics.yaml: new metrics (obs.anomaly.snr, obs.anomaly.anchor_count, obs.log.summary_length). 4) ui/operator/dashboard/operator_anomaly_queue.json: new dashboard showing prioritized queue with SNR, tenant drift sparkline, recent summaries, and quick links to traces. 5) infra/helm/values.yaml: feature flag for staged rollout and canary config. 6) docs/observability/anomaly_operators.md: operator playbook and escalation steps. 7) tests/replaybench/anomaly_replay_test.go and unit tests for summarizer.

small_snippets:
Example summarizer template used to produce TL;DR: 

- input logs (30s window) -> extract top-4 frequent tokens, top exception/error lines, top 2 stack frames, response time percentiles -> output: '[ANOMALY] saw 3x token-cost spike; spike started at +00:00:12; top error: TimeoutError in kernel_dispatch; median resp 120ms -> 900ms (p95)'.
testing: Unit tests for summarizer (coverage ~86%), replaybench scenario that replays historical anomaly traces against the processor, and an end-to-end smoke test that verifies TLDR items appear on the operator dashboard. E2E: flaky at first due to a race in the replaybench; fixed by adding a small debounce in the processor. CI matrix: build/linters passing, unit tests passing, integration/replaybench passing on rerun.
rollout_plan: Feature flag-controlled. Stage 1: enable on canary cluster (internal) for 48 hours. Stage 2: enable for 50% of hosted traffic (by tenant bucket) and monitor obs.anomaly.snr and obs.log.summary_length for regressions; Stage 3: 100% with default alerting policy. We will run a one-week observational window before enabling high-priority auto-suppression rules. A manual rollback plan is documented in docs/observability/anomaly_operators.md.
privacy_and_cost_considerations: Summaries are compact strings and the processor retains only the pre-aggregated context by default. By default we do not persist full raw logs for summaries; raw retention is controlled by tenant settings. The sidecar summarizer runs at edge with CPU-bound workloads; cost impact is expected to be minor (<2% CPU per node in canary).

notes_for_oncall: Oncall: watch obs.anomaly.snr for sudden drops (indicates summarizer failure) and obs.log.summary_length trending up (could indicate overly verbose summaries). Playbook steps are in docs/observability/anomaly_operators.md.
